description: Issuers whose ticker string differs between sources, anchored to the identifiers that did NOT change (CIK / ISIN / composite FIGI). `alias_to_canonical` maps any known symbol to the coverage universe ticker; `vendor_symbols` gives the symbol to send a named vendor. This file does not assert which symbol is 'current' — no source reliably says, which is why the join is aliased rather than rewritten.

entries.note: The two directions are genuinely opposed, which is why vendor_symbols is per-vendor rather than one 'true' symbol: yfinance serves only FISV, FINRA's short-interest series is keyed FI. Two published surfaces were corrupted in opposite directions: portfolio_daily could not join the broker's FISV to this row's FI, so the characteristics table warned 'not in the CM perf frame (no fundamentals): FISV' and the PUBLIC page invented an 'Unclassified' sector bucket holding this name alone; insider_ownership asked yfinance for FI and rendered every Fiserv stake as a share count with no dollar value. NOT this: portfolio_daily's 'no short-interest data: FISV' warning. Measured 2026-08-27, yfinance returns every short-interest field as null for BOTH FISV and FI (that lane reads yfinance .info, not FINRA), so it is a real vendor gap and the alias does not fix it. Entered 2026-08-27 for board row #345.

entries.note: Entered 2026-09-06. CSU reached the portfolio workbook on 2026-09-05 when the CM->sheet sync pulled in 21 Following-for-Interest names that had never had a row, and it was the only one of the 21 with no price: every refresh logged 'CSU: no price available' and the run went DEGRADED. ⚠ CSU.TO QUOTES IN CAD. The workbook's Last Price column carries no currency, so this price sits beside USD ones -- as 2715.HK's HKD price already does. Harmless for a Watchlist name (no Mkt Value, weight or cost basis is computed from it) and NOT harmless if this name is ever bought: the sizing block would read a CAD cost basis against a USD book. See the fleet rule that a number cannot state its own unit.
